Recommend HUD Action:
Several alternative plans were developed for the Urban Renewal Area. These plans and their concepts were discussed in detail in the DEIS. The plan that was found to be most acceptable and allowed a great amount of flexibility was the Neighborhood Plan known here—in as the "Preferred Plan". Also with the flexibility of this plan, options may be exercised by the CRA in the development of the parcels, Development of the "Preferred Plan" shall follow the "Revised Amendment No. 1" of the Urban Renewal Plan dated 10-31-77 and attached herein as Exhibit "AA". This plan has been approved by HUD.
Environmentally the project is considered acceptable. Its proposed benefits outweigh its probable adverse impacts. The environmental deficiencies that existed before the Urban Renewal activities began would have persisted and most likely worsened.
Therefore it is the recommendation of HUD that the "Preferred Plan" be accepted and put into execution with the following special conditions:
1. Residential / Hotel buildings, if constructed, shall be set back from the street line and noise attenuating measures shall be incorporated into their design to meet HUD Circular 1390.2. Controls to mitigate noise to residential/hotel development shall be enforced by the CRA. 
2. The CRA shall include all necessary and appropriate controls to mitigage noise during construction in its contract with developers.
3. The CRA shall insure that energy conservation measures be designed into the building structure as well as its energy units.
4. The CRA shall follow, 'Measures to minimize adverse impacts and enhance environmental quality," as outlined on pages II-4-17 & II-4-18 of the DEIS.
5. The CRA shall take into consideration the MHC's comment regarding the review of the design plans by the Cambridge Historical Commission regarding the use of materials to highlight historic development.
